input.brief: Quanela: one place where a Colombian food business runs its day — the order (counter, phone, web menu, WhatsApp) travels through the kitchen and delivery and lands in stock, recipe cost and receivables; AI agents recommend over that real data

direction.name: The split stage
direction.idea: Half the screen never moves. One side is a fixed photograph (or object, or product view) that stays in place for the whole visit; the other side is a calm scrolling column with everything you need to read. The fixed half keeps the feeling present while the reader gets on with the facts, like sitting in the room while reading the menu. As sections pass, the fixed image may quietly change to the one that matches.
direction.composition: Desktop: a two-column page, 50/50 or 45/55. One column is `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` and holds a single photograph filling it edge to edge, or the object centred on a flat field. The other column scrolls and holds all content in a single narrow measure (max 46ch) with comfortable padding (48–72px): name and one-line description first, then sections separated by generous space, then contact and footer. Headings in the scrolling column are modest (32–44px). The column grounds differ: photograph on one side, flat paper colour on the other, meeting at a clean vertical edge. On a phone the fixed half becomes a 60svh image at the top that stays sticky behind the first section, then releases.
direction.typography: A text-first setting: a readable serif or a calm sans at 17–19px, with one display size for the name. Left-aligned throughout.
direction.colour: The paper colour of the reading column is chosen against the photograph: a tone taken from its shadows or its lightest area. One ink, optionally one accent ink for links and the action.
direction.imagery: One excellent portrait-orientation photograph for the fixed half, plus three or four more that crossfade in as their sections arrive. Small inline photographs in the reading column are optional and should be few.
direction.richness: A full-height photograph always in view, against a quiet, well-set column of text.
direction.pitfalls: The reading column must be genuinely well typeset, since it is half the page. Do not put cards or grids in it. Check that the fixed image crops well at short viewport heights. In blind tests the commonest complaint was monotony: several screens of the same split with only the text changing. Change what the reading half holds from section to section (a list, a large figure, a table, a full-colour panel, a drawing) and let at least one section break the split and run full width.

hero.name: Inset photograph, crossing wordmark
hero.blueprint: One deep, dark flat field. A tall portrait photograph fills the left 47% of the viewport, inset 20px from the top, left and bottom edges, with a 12px radius and object-fit: cover; it is position: sticky for the length of the page while the right side scrolls. Five text links at 15px sit top-right on a 32px margin, the last of them the single action. There is no logo at the top. In the right half, at 44% of the height and centred on that half's own axis, one supporting sentence in the light ink at 24px on up to three lines, max 26ch. Along the bottom runs the name in lowercase at clamp(120px, 12vw, 200px), light or regular weight, tracking -0.04em, on one line. It starts over the photograph's lower-right corner, overlapping the image by about 10% of the viewport width (z-index above it; mix-blend-mode: difference keeps the letters legible on the picture), and ends flush with the right margin, its baseline 40px above the bottom edge.
hero.mobile: The photograph takes the top 58% of the screen, inset 12px, with the same radius. The name runs under it at 21vw on one line, its ascenders overlapping the photograph's bottom edge by 3vw. The sentence follows at 17px, left-aligned on a 20px margin. Links reduce to a menu word and the action on the top row, set over the photograph.
hero.headline: The name in lowercase on one line, up to 9 characters at this size; a longer name drops to 9vw.

photos.title: Fog and quiet
photos.note: misty, muted, minimal landscapes and empty horizons; calm areas for text

photos.alt: Misty river winding through a grassy valley between forested slopes
Lone marker post standing in still water wrapped in fog
Road lined with tall trees fading into thick fog
Still misty water fading into a soft pink-grey sky

motion.name: Scaling wordmark
motion.description: The giant name responds to the scroll: as the first screen leaves, the wordmark scales down a few percent (or grows from 0.94 to 1 as the footer arrives) on a scroll-linked timeline, so the monument feels heavy. Travel stays under 8%. Static fallback where scroll timelines are unsupported. Recipe: 'Scroll-linked progress' in references/motion.md, animating `scale`.

sections.name: Output index, live sheet
sections.blueprint: For products that make documents: invoices, reports, emails, statements. Columns 1–5 list the names of three to five outputs, one per line, at clamp(36px, 4vw, 64px), leading 1.1, each a `<button>`; the selected name is in full ink, the rest in the soft ink. There is no other heading. Columns 7–12 are a stage in a flat tone one step from the ground, 88svh tall, and on it lies the selected output as an object: a paper-white sheet 560px wide, built in HTML at true size, root marked data-ui, with a real sender, real line items, sums that add up and a date. The sheet starts 72px below the stage's top and runs past its bottom edge, which crops it. Selecting a name swaps the sheet with a 200ms crossfade; an email is narrower (440px), a receipt narrower still (300px), all left-aligned 64px into the stage.
sections.mobile: Names become one sideways-scrolling row at 22px with scroll-snap, the selected one in full ink. Beneath, the stage fills the width and is 70svh tall; the sheet keeps its true size, anchored top-left with a 16px inset and cropped by the stage's right and bottom edges. Tapping a name swaps it.

sections.name: Drag through the stages
sections.blueprint: A 50/50 split, 88svh tall: two flat fields meeting on a clean vertical edge, and one slider that drives both. Left field: the current stage as a clause of three to six words at clamp(40px, 4.6vw, 76px) on two lines, top-left from column 1, starting with its order word; it serves as the heading. Right field: one fragment of the product at true size, about 440px wide, centred, root marked data-ui, in the state that matches the clause. Along the bottom, crossing both fields inside 28px margins, a real range `<input>` with four stops: a solid track 8px tall, the part already passed in full ink, and a square thumb 32px across in the accent. Under the track, four stage names at 16px, the current one in full ink. Dragging, or the arrow keys, swaps the clause and the fragment's state with a 200ms crossfade; nothing depends on scroll.
sections.mobile: The fragment's field comes first, 46svh, the fragment at true size and cropped to its active region. The slider follows directly beneath on the seam, thumb 40px. Then the clause field: the clause at 9vw on two lines, with the four stage names under it in a two-by-two block at 15px.

sections.name: Small proof beside text
sections.blueprint: One narrow module repeated four to six times down the page, never alternating sides. Each module is 640px wide at most and starts on the page's text margin (at about 22% of the viewport on an understated page). Left part: a flat panel 360px wide and 120 to 200px tall, one tone off the ground, radius 8px, holding one small exact demonstration: a cropped interface fragment at true size, or a tightly cropped photograph covering the panel. Right part, 20px away and top-aligned: a heading of one or two lines at 18px medium and two short paragraphs at 15px in the soft ink, in a column 250px wide. Panel heights vary with their content; text always hangs from the panel's top edge. 96–120px of empty ground between modules. The section heading is 24–28px, on the same left edge, 64px above the first module. In a column under 600px the text moves beneath its panel.
sections.mobile: Each module stacks: the panel at full width and natural height, then heading and paragraphs 16px below on the same left edge, at 17px and 15px. 64px between modules. Panels keep their true-size contents and crop from the right instead of scaling down.

sections.name: Two plans, two fields
sections.blueprint: Two plans stand side by side as two full-height colour fields that meet at a hard vertical edge with no gap: the left field spans columns 1–5, the right 6–12, both 90svh tall and bleeding to the viewport edges. Each field has its own flat colour and its assigned text colour. Inside each, on a shared grid: the plan name at about 5vw top-left with 40px padding; one sentence at 20px beneath it, no wider than 26ch, saying who the plan is for; then, anchored to the bottom-left, the price at about 10vw with the period at 18px beside it; and a rectangular button anchored bottom-right on the price's baseline. What is included is written as a short paragraph, not a tick list. The unequal widths say which plan matters more without any badge. No heading spans the two fields.
sections.mobile: The fields stack, each 70svh tall, the more important plan first. Name at 12vw top-left, sentence beneath, price at 24vw at the bottom-left, and the button full width along the bottom edge inside 20px padding. The hard colour edge between the two is kept.

sections.name: Answers as reading text
sections.blueprint: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme. A heading of two or three words at 28–32px sits in columns 1–3, top-aligned. Columns 5–12 hold the text in two columns (`columns: 2; column-gap: 56px`), each about 36ch wide, at 16–17px with leading 1.55. Each item is one paragraph: the question is the opening run-in, set in the medium weight in the full ink and ending with its question mark, and the answer continues on the same line in the regular weight. Paragraphs are separated by 20px and carry `break-inside: avoid` so none splits across columns. No toggles, no icons, no boxes. Eight to fourteen items fit on one screen, which is the point: everything is answered at a glance. Where the page's reading column is narrow, use one column.
sections.mobile: One column at 16px with 20px margins. The heading leads at 24px. Each paragraph keeps its run-in question in the medium weight, with 18px between paragraphs. The section may run to two screens; do not collapse it into an accordion.

sections.name: First step, already open
sections.blueprint: The page ends with the product's first screen already open. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, 90svh tall. Right, in columns 7–11, vertically centred: the product's own create dialog at true size, 440px wide, root marked data-ui, with its real title ('Name your workspace'), one text field holding an editable, believable example, one two-option segmented choice and its primary button. Inside the fragment the product's conventions apply, including the shadow its dialog normally casts. The field accepts typing, the choice switches, and the primary button is the page's only action: it carries the typed value into sign-up. Left, in columns 1–5, anchored to the bottom with 40px margins: the closing line, two to four words at clamp(56px, 7vw, 112px), leading 0.92, on two lines, and under it one sentence at 17px saying what happens after the button. The upper-left stays empty.
sections.mobile: The closing line leads at 13vw on two lines, top-left, with its sentence beneath at 16px. The dialog follows at full width inside 16px margins, at true size, its primary button 52px tall and full width. The field is at least 84svh; the dialog sits in its lower half.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Rafael Derolez
references.idea: A portfolio as a phone carousel: a fixed text rail on the left narrates whichever phone-shaped screen is centred on the right.
references.hero: Dark charcoal page split by a vertical hairline at 30% width. Left rail: a 55px header row with name, slash and current section as a breadcrumb in 16px sans, plus a small cobalt ticket-shaped hire button with a perforated divider and arrow; below a hairline, four short paragraphs of 16px grey text with white links, top-aligned, leaving the lower 40% of the rail empty. Right 70%: three phone-proportioned frames with large rounded corners in a row; the centre one upright, full brightness and about 680px tall, the outer two smaller, dimmed and rotated in perspective toward the centre.
references.type: Suisse at a single 16px size, weight 400, for everything; hierarchy comes only from grey versus white and from the breadcrumb. The one larger setting is a bold two-word line inside the blue contact card. No display type at all.
references.colour: #18181b #030303 #969696 #173ded #ffffff — Zinc-black field with grey text and white for links and the active breadcrumb. Cobalt blue appears only on the hire button and contact card; all other colour comes from the app screenshots.
references.imagery: Phone-shaped frames with large corner radius holding app screens, a selfie and short videos; side frames are dimmed to about 40% and tilted in 3D like a cover-flow.
references.layout: Single viewport, no page scroll: a fixed 432px text rail with 32px padding and a media stage filling the rest. Scrolling advances the carousel and replaces the rail's text; hairlines separate rail, header and stage. On mobile the stage stacks above the rail.

sections.description: Same two-part frame. The breadcrumb's last word changes to the project name; under the header sit three tiny grey meta tags (employer, platform), then two paragraphs. On the stage the centred phone shows the product screen at full brightness while neighbours show the previous and next items dimmed and tilted, so the carousel works as both navigation and preview.

In the rail, a cobalt card shaped like a ticket with notched sides: tiny labels top-left and top-right, a large bold two-word heading, name and local time in small text, then a perforated lower strip with email at left and a copy button at right. Under it, a career list: company in white with dates in small grey on one line, role on the next, and a small arrow at the far right of each row.

steal: Use a breadcrumb (name / current item) as the only heading and update its last word as the content changes.
Show work in device-shaped frames arranged as a cover-flow, with neighbours dimmed and tilted so the next item is always previewed.
Shape the contact card like a ticket with notches and a perforated strip so the one accent-colour element feels like an object.

references.name: Le Petit Bleu
references.idea: The cafe's teal-and-white stripes become the whole system: one teal ink on cream, everything boxed in thin double outlines like printed menu cards, beside a permanently visible photo of the room.
references.hero: Viewport split 50/50 with 12px gaps. Left: a cream panel with a thin pale-teal outline and rounded corners. Inside, a second outlined box is the nav bar: two-line hamburger left, teal brush-script logo about 300px wide centred, a caps order link right. Below, a two-line light serif headline at about 3.5vw, centred, in teal, then two centred stacks, each a bold caps label, a serif line and a solid teal button wrapped in a second thin outline. Right: a full-height rounded photo of a striped booth, with an outlined hours bar across its top, three slide dots bottom-left and a white address card bottom-right.
references.type: Self Modern, a light bookish serif, for headline and 15px body; Matter SQ bold caps for labels and buttons; Archive Mono Pro typewriter caps for menu rows; a brush-script logo. Section titles are tall condensed serif caps sized so four to seven letters fill the column.
references.colour: #fcfbf7 #13a7b2 #058599 #cfe5e7 #e9b81f — Cream paper and a single teal used for every word, rule, outline and button; no black anywhere. Yellow, floral reds and marble enter only through the interior photographs.
references.imagery: Bright, saturated interior and food photographs; the right-hand panel is a full-height slideshow with rounded corners. Small food shots sit in a horizontal strip, and a fine line drawing of the shopfront with one teal awning fills a card.
references.layout: The left half scrolls as a stack of outlined cream cards (full-width or two-up) with 12px gaps while the right half stays fixed. Card contents are centred. A sticky nav card rides over the stack. On mobile the photo becomes the hero card's background.

sections.description: A card containing only the section word in tall condensed serif caps, teal, sized so its four letters fill the column edge to edge. Below it, a stack of full-width outlined rows about 36px high, each with a category name in typewriter mono caps at left and a thin plus sign at right, separated by 6px gaps. Above the title: a ticker row of tiny caps and a strip of four small food photos with rounded corners.

The same giant condensed title treatment, then centred serif paragraphs in teal with underlined links in a narrow measure of about 280px. Further down, a landscape photo of the two proprietors with a centred two-line caption in tiny sans, followed by more centred paragraphs. All of it lives in the left half while the right photo panel has advanced to a shelf-wall image.

A header row with a tiny bold caps label at left and a script follow-us link with arrow at right, then three portrait images (about 3:5) with 12px rounded corners in a row, the third cropped by the column edge to imply a carousel. Directly below, the next giant section title begins and is cropped by the viewport.

steal: Print everything in one brand ink on cream, including body text, rules and buttons, and let photographs supply the other colours.
Wrap buttons and panels in a second thin outline offset by a few pixels to get a printed-ticket feel.
Keep a tall photo panel fixed on one half and scroll a stack of cards on the other, swapping the photo as sections change.

references.name: Juggle
references.idea: The headline literally drowns: a flat blue field rises to half height and the lines below the waterline turn from red to submerged navy.
references.hero: Two flat fields: white above, saturated blue below, meeting at exactly half height. A three-line all-caps headline in a black-weight grotesque at 8.4vw is centred across the seam, about 65% of the width, lines nearly touching. The first line sits on white in red-orange; the second is cut by the seam, and its lower half plus the whole third line render dark navy as if under water. Small red logo top-left, a rectangular red button with tracked caps top-right. Near the bottom, one line of white condensed caps names the audience. No image, no sub-paragraph.
references.type: Acme Gothic Black 900 caps at 122px, -0.03em, for the hero only. Section heads use Helvetica Now Display Condensed bold caps around 48 to 70px; body is Helvetica Now 17px; labels are small tracked caps. Roughly a 7:1 headline-to-body jump.
references.colour: #2e2eff #ffffff #ff3b1f #0a0a0a #f5f3ef #020156 — Three flat poster colours each own whole sections: electric blue, red-orange and black, with white and warm off-white for product areas. No tints, no gradients.
references.imagery: Simplified product UI on a cream rounded panel over black with a small video-call window; otherwise flat vector graphics: a pair of blinking eyes, a smiley cut into shuffled square tiles.
references.layout: Full-bleed colour blocks with one message each, mostly centred. Product sections switch to a two-column split on off-white with about 90px margins. Marquee strips separate blocks and a slim sticky bar carrying the CTA rides the bottom edge.

sections.description: Full-screen electric blue. Centred stack: a tiny tracked caps label, three lines of white condensed bold caps at about 5vw, a gap, then a single heavier, wider word at a larger size as the punchline, a faint blurred line of text beneath it and an outlined rectangular button. Wide empty margins left and right.

Problem check on full-screen red-orange, under a white marquee strip of condensed caps with small red buttons repeating inside it. Centre: a two-line white condensed caps heading at about 5vw; below, a flat illustration of two white almond eyes with black pupils; a tracked caps instruction line; then three evenly spaced white outlined checkboxes, each with a two-line caption, one already ticked.

Black section. A small tracked caps title centred, under it three numbered text tabs in a row with the active one underlined. Below, a cream rounded app window about 55% wide fills the rest of the viewport: mostly blank note area, a floating status chip, and a small dark video-call window with three faces overlapping its lower edge.

White. Left: a narrow column of small body text, two founder names with roles, then three link columns under tracked caps labels. Right: a blue square about 280px holding a white smiley face sliced into a three-by-three grid of tiles that are rotated and shuffled like a sliding puzzle. Tiny logo and copyright bottom-left.

steal: Split the hero into two flat colour fields and recolour the headline where it crosses the seam, so the layout acts out the copy.
Give each section one saturated flat colour and one sentence, and separate them with a thin marquee strip.
Turn a pain-point list into a mock checklist with real checkboxes under a blunt question heading.
